A reliable handover between the tools you already use

You don’t have to replace every system to reduce double-handling. The useful first project is often one connection: an enquiry becoming a job, a completed job reaching the office, or approved information becoming ready for invoicing.

I map that handover with you, check what your platforms support and build a connection around the way your team works. That can involve an API integration, a supported automation platform or a small custom tool. The approach follows the problem and the access your software provides.

What a first project could cover

  • Enquiries into your job system. Capture the details once, flag missing information and prepare a record for your team to review.
  • Job information back to the office. Pass approved completion details to the next stage without retyping a technician’s notes.
  • Customer records that agree. Decide which system owns each field and how updates are shared.
  • Visible failures. Make a failed transfer something your team can find and resolve, rather than a missing job discovered later.

These are examples to scope, not promises of compatibility with every product. API access, subscription tiers, export formats and platform restrictions all affect what can be connected.

How we get from a workaround to a working connection

  1. Follow one real job. Show me where information starts, where it goes and where somebody copies it.
  2. Agree the rules. Choose the source of truth, approvals, duplicate handling and what should happen when data is incomplete.
  3. Build and test the handover. Try ordinary jobs, repeated submissions and failed connections before relying on it.
  4. Make support clear. Agree who monitors the connection, how errors are handled and how changes to either platform are maintained.

Does the connection need AI?

Sometimes. An unstructured email may need interpretation; an approved customer address usually needs a dependable transfer. I can use AI workflow automation for the interpretation step and ordinary integration for moving structured records.

Start with the handover that wastes the most time

For our first conversation, bring the names of your systems and one example of the double-handling, with customer details removed. We can meet in Melbourne or talk remotely. I’ll help you work out whether a connection is feasible and what a defined first project would involve.

A few practical questions

Can you connect my current job management and accounting software?

I’ll check the exact products and plans first. A supported API or export is usually needed. Some platforms restrict access, so compatibility is confirmed before a build is scoped.

Will I need to change software?

Not necessarily. The goal is to keep the tools that work and improve the handover. If the platform itself is the problem, we can separately assess a replacement.

How much does systems integration cost?

The scope depends on the systems, number of handovers, data quality, error handling and ongoing support. We agree the work and its cost before starting; subscription or API fees need to be counted too.
